subtopics.title: Mean, median and mode
subtopics.exposition: The mean of a set of values is the sum of the values divided by the number of values in the set. The median of a data set is the value in the central position when the data set has been arranged from the lowest to the highest value. The mode of a data set is the value that occurs most often in the set. The mode can also be described as the most frequent or most common value in the data set. For a data set {x1; x2; ...; xn}, the mean x-bar equals (1/n) times the sum of the values xi for i from 1 to n, which is (x1 + x2 + ... + xn) divided by n. Exactly half of the values in a data set are less than the median and the other half are greater than the median. If there is an odd number of values in the data set, the median is equal to one of the values in the data set. If there is an even number of values in the data set, the median lies halfway between two values in the data set. A data set can have more than one mode if more than one value has the highest count; for example, both 2 and 3 are modes of the data set {1; 2; 2; 3; 3}. To calculate the median of a quantitative data set, first sort the data from the smallest to the largest value and then find the value in the middle. To calculate the mode, count the number of times that each value appears in the data set and then find the value that appears most often. To find the mean of {10; 20; 30; 40; 50}, first calculate the sum of the data: 10 + 20 + 30 + 40 + 50 = 150. Then divide the sum by the number of values in the data set: with 5 values, the mean is 150 divided by 5, which is 30. To find the median of {10; 14; 86; 2; 68; 99; 1}, first sort the values from the smallest to the largest: 1; 2; 10; 14; 68; 86; 99. With an odd number of values (7), the median is the value in the middle, in the fourth position, so the median of this data set is 14. With an even number of values (8, sorted as 1; 2; 10; 11; 14; 68; 86; 99), the median is halfway between the values in the fourth and fifth positions, 11 and 14, so the median is (11 + 14)/2 = 12.5. To find the mode of {2; 2; 3; 4; 4; 4; 6; 6; 7; 8; 8; 10; 10}, first count the number of times each value appears in the data set. Then find the value that appears most often: 4 is the only value that appears 3 times and all the other values appear fewer than 3 times, so the mode is 4. The mean of a set of values is written with a horizontal bar over the variable that represents the set, for example x-bar. The mean is sometimes also called the average or the arithmetic mean. If all points in a data set occur with equal frequency, it is equally accurate to describe the data set as having many modes or as having no mode.

subtopics.title: Interpreting measures in context
subtopics.exposition: Continuous values can lie anywhere on the real line, so any particular value will almost never repeat. For a continuous data set, the frequency of each value will be 1, so there will be no mode. A data set is quantitative if each value can be represented by a number; the bread masses are therefore quantitative data. Since a mass can be any real number, the bread-mass data are continuous. To find the mean for each day (each column) of continuous measurements, add up the measurements and divide by the number of measurements, which is 10 here; for Monday the sum is 8007.9, so the mean is 800.8 g. To find the median for each day, sort the numbers from lowest to highest and find the value in the middle. With an even number of measurements (10), the median is halfway between the two numbers in the middle; for Monday these are 801.2 and 802.3, so the median is 801.8 g. In the bread data the means and medians for the days of the week are close to one another, but not quite equal. Since the bread data are continuous, the mode cannot be computed. To judge the data against a regulation, first work out the allowed range from the stated leeway: an unlabelled loaf must weigh 800 g, with 5 percent under allowed (760 g) and 10 percent over allowed (880 g), so the allowed range is 760 g to 880 g. The supplier is judged to meet the requirement because every measurement lies within the allowed range and the means and medians are all close to 800 g. From the bread data the book concludes that the supplier is reliable. In the bread example the means and medians are given correct to 1 decimal place.

subtopics.title: Effect of outliers
subtopics.exposition: An outlier is a value in the data set that is not typical of the rest of the set. An outlier is usually a value that is much greater or much less than all the other values in the data set. In general, the median is less affected by the addition of outliers to a data set than the mean is. To see the effect of an outlier, compare the mean and median of the data set before and after the outlier is included. Including the outlier of 181 cm changes the mean height from 155.9 cm to 158.2 cm, a change of 2.3 cm. Before the outlier is added, the 10 sorted values have a median halfway between the fifth and sixth values, (156 + 157)/2 = 156.5 cm. After the outlier is added, there are 11 values and the median is the sixth value, 157 cm. The median changes by only 0.5 cm when the outlier is added, compared with a change of 2.3 cm for the mean.
